nodes.description: The initiating lesion in the alleles that the isoform model explains. A premature termination codon or a structural change inside COL2A1 exon 2 removes or destabilises the exon 2 containing transcript from that allele. Reported alleles include Cys64Stop and Cys57Tyr, a Cys86 premature termination codon in an eight-generation pedigree, and C192A. Lymphoblast RT-PCR in a Cys64Stop patient recovered only the normal allele's IIA form, which the reporting authors read as either nonsense-mediated decay of the mutant IIA transcript or nonsense-associated skipping of exon 2 - in either case, no mutant IIA product.

nodes.description: The congenital half of the ocular phenotype, and the finding an ophthalmic examination can see directly. The type 1 membranous vitreous phenotype is specific enough to COL2A1 that it has been used as a screening gate - a 50-family series selected on the membranous phenotype alone found COL2A1 mutations in 94 percent of cases. Vitreous syneresis was present in every affected individual of the largest pedigree.

nodes.description: The vitreous is the only adult tissue containing procollagen IIA, so it absorbs the whole effect of an isoform-restricted null allele. The consequence for the gel is structural rather than metabolic - the heterotypic type II/XI collagen fibril network that holds the vitreous gel together is built from fewer alpha-1(II) chains.

nodes.description: The step that makes this a distinct disease rather than a mild Stickler syndrome. COL2A1 pre-mRNA is alternatively spliced into a long isoform that retains exon 2 (type IIA) and a short isoform that skips it (type IIB). The two are expressed in different tissues, so an exon 2 lesion partitions along that boundary instead of reducing type II collagen everywhere. This is the node the whole entity turns on, and it has no counterpart in classic type 1 Stickler syndrome, where the lesion is not isoform-selective.

nodes.description: The branch that explains an absence, which is why it is drawn. Adult differentiated chondrocytes express the exon 2 skipping IIB isoform almost exclusively, so a premature termination codon inside exon 2 is not present in the transcript they make. The cartilage, and with it the arthropathy, craniofacial and auditory features of classic type 1 Stickler syndrome, is largely spared. This node deliberately has no downstream edge: what it produces is the non-occurrence of the systemic phenotype, and drawing an arrow to an absent manifestation would be a phantom node.

Note the strength of the underlying evidence is not established here - the guidance is a management recommendation for Stickler syndrome, and no controlled trial restricted to the ocular-only variant is cited in this entry.

nodes.description: The outcome that dominates management. Stickler syndrome is the commonest inherited cause of childhood rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, the tear is frequently a giant retinal tear, it is commonly bilateral, and it is a frequent cause of blindness. In the largest ocular-only pedigree, 70 percent of detachments occurred between 4 and 18 years of age, which is why surveillance has to start in childhood rather than at presentation.
